+# Public pages
+
+The dashboard serves four pages without a session, all under `/-/`:
+
+| Page | Source of truth | Gate |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `/-/pricing` | `internal/hosted/publicsite.Plans` | `ValidatePlans`; a test keeps `web/dashboard/lib/pricing.json` identical |
+| `/-/docs` | Files in `docs/` at the deployed commit | Links only; no copied prose |
+| `/-/changelog` | Repository `CHANGELOG.md` | `ParseChangelog`: dated sections newest first, one merged-PR link per entry |
+| `/-/status` | `/status.json` on the `web` role | Readiness probes only |
+
+## Why `/-/`
+
+Dashboard routes start with the organization login (`/:organization/...`).
+GitHub and GitLab both reject logins that begin with `-`, so `/-/` can never
+shadow a tenant's dashboard. A bare `/pricing` would hide the dashboard of a
+real organization named `pricing`.
+
+## Pricing
+
+One standard review costs one credit. Starter includes 50 credits a month for
+one developer; Pro is $0.80 per credit, shared across the organization, with no
+seat fees; approved open-source repositories are free; Enterprise is an annual
+contract. Review tiers are not priced until they ship.
+
+`MaxStandardReviewCostMicrousd` derives the model-cost ceiling that keeps a Pro
+review at or above the 60% margin guardrail: $0.32. The v1 cost target of
+$0.40 per median review is above that ceiling, so it would trigger margin
+alerts at list price.
+
+## Status
+
+The status response contains component names, `operational` or `unavailable`,
+and the check time. It never includes error text, latency, hosts, or tenant
+data. A component is operational only when its readiness endpoint answers 2xx
+within two seconds without redirects. If the dashboard cannot reach
+`PX1_STATUS_URL`, the page says status could not be checked and makes no
+claim about health.
+
+## Changelog
+
+Add one line per merged pull request under its UTC merge date:
+
+```markdown
+## 2026-10-29
+
+- Add auditable requirement coverage ([#221](https://github.com/kedarvartak/px1/pull/221))
+```
+
+Free-form lines inside a dated section fail the test, so the published page
+cannot drift from the file.

explanations.title: Serve status from the web role
explanations.summary: Only the web role serves the unauthenticated `/status.json` endpoint, using the component list from `PX1_STATUS_COMPONENTS`; invalid configuration prevents the service from starting.

explanations.title: Add tenant-free public routes
explanations.summary: The dashboard now reserves `/-/` for four public pages—pricing, docs, changelog, and status—so those URLs do not overlap organization-scoped routes.

explanations.title: Report status from readiness probes
explanations.summary: Status is based on configured readiness URLs: each component is operational only if its endpoint returns 2xx within two seconds, and redirects count as unavailable. URLs must use HTTPS, except for loopback HTTP; probe details are omitted from the response, and an empty component list reports unavailable.

explanations.title: Publish linked release history
explanations.summary: The public changelog groups entries by UTC date and links each entry to its pull request. The parser rejects malformed dates, duplicate pull requests, and entries without matching links, with a test validating the repository changelog.

explanations.title: Link to product documentation
explanations.summary: The public docs page links to installation, delivery, metrics, configuration, privacy, retention, and terms documents in the repository, rather than duplicating their contents.

explanations.title: Publish hosted pricing
explanations.summary: Visitors can see the plans and credit pricing: Starter includes 50 monthly credits, Pro costs $0.80 per credit, qualified open-source repositories can get free credits, and Enterprise requires contacting sales. The plan data is checked against the Go pricing table by a test.

explanations.title: Show checked status without guessing
explanations.summary: The public status page fetches `/status.json` without caching. If the URL is unset or the fetch fails, it says status could not be checked instead of claiming services are healthy or down.
